name: Salary
definition: Annual cash pay for the job.

name: Personal Budget
definition: Annual personal work-expense budget for approved client travel, meals, lodging, and related sales costs.

name: Starting Date
definition: The calendar date when the candidate begins the job.

name: Probation Length
definition: Length of the initial probation period.

name: Contract Length
definition: Length of the fixed-term employment contract.

name: Vacation Days
definition: Number of paid vacation days each year.

name: Remote Working Days
definition: Number of regular workdays each week that may be worked remotely.
aliases: work from home three days a week

name: Professional Training Program
definition: Whether the company funds an external professional training program.
aliases: the company pays for relevant courses
I cover my own training costs if needed

name: Mentorship Program
definition: Whether the company assigns the candidate an experienced internal mentor.
aliases: I would like an internal mentor
the company should assign me a mentor
mentoring should be available but optional

name: Role in Recruitment Fair
definition: Whether the candidate represents the company at a recruitment fair.
aliases: I can attend one recruiting fair a year
I do not want regular recruiting-fair duty
I could represent the company at several fairs

name: Mandatory Conference Presentations
definition: Whether the candidate must present at professional conferences for the company.
aliases: I can give one conference talk each year
I do not want speaking to be mandatory
the role should include several conference presentations

name: Non-compete Clause
definition: Whether the company waives its standard non-compete clause.
aliases: I need freedom to join a competitor later
I will not accept a twelve-month non-compete

name: Professional Associations Membership
definition: Whether the company pays the candidate's fee for one relevant professional association.
aliases: the company should pay my professional membership dues
I will pay the association fees myself

name: Role in Organizing Social Events
definition: Whether the candidate must organize company social events.
aliases: I can help with occasional team events
I do not want to organize social events
regular event planning should not be part of my role

name: Regular Social Media Posts for Company
definition: How much of the usual company social-media posting workload the employee commits to: 0 means no commitment and 1 means the full usual commitment. Exact fractions are scored proportionally.
unit: share of the usual company social-media posting workload
aliases: I do not want LinkedIn posting to be part of my role

commitment_scale.basis: Share of the usual posting workload, not a count of posts with an unstated baseline.
commitment_scale.interpretation_note: Slightly less means 75% of usual workload; less or reduced means 50%; minimal means 25%. These are researcher-set conventions, shown for participant review. An explicit percentage takes precedence.

name: Commission on Customer Payments
definition: Percentage of customer money actually received on sales credited to the candidate and paid as commission.

name: New-Hire Ramp Guarantee
definition: Guaranteed extra pay during the first three months that is never deducted from later commissions.
unit: US dollars paid during the first three months

name: Commission Payment Schedule
definition: How often earned commission is paid after the customer pays the company.

name: Expense Repayment Speed
definition: Maximum time to repay approved business expenses after complete documentation is received.

name: Commission Reversal Period
definition: Time after payment during which commission may be reversed for customer cancellation, refund, or nonpayment.
aliases: when paid commission can be taken back

name: Above-Target Commission Rate
definition: Commission rate applied to individual sales above the agreed target.

name: Commission Starting Point
definition: Eligible annual sales amount required before commission payments begin.
unit: US dollars of eligible annual sales

name: Home Office Setup Payment
definition: One-time company payment toward approved furniture and ergonomic equipment for an agreed home-working arrangement.

name: Starting Bonus
definition: One-time payment made when employment begins, separate from salary and future commission.
unit: US dollars paid once at employment start

name: Performance-Based Bonus
definition: One-time cash bonus when an agreed individual or team performance target is reached. This is separate from a sign-on payment, a salary increase, commission and a contract-renewal bonus. Individual and team targets use the same bonus-payoff scale.
unit: US dollars paid once if the agreed performance target is reached

name: Credential Completion Payment
definition: One-time payment for completing one company-approved, role-relevant external credential during employment.
unit: US dollars paid once after verified completion

name: Scheduled Salary Increase
definition: Percentage increase to base salary paid after completing eighteen months of employment.

name: Early Sales Target
definition: Share of the normal sales target expected during the first 90 days.
unit: percent of normal sales target during first 90 days
aliases: How much of the normal target applies at first?
Could the early target be lower while I learn the role?
Would the full target start immediately?

name: Feedback Meeting Frequency
definition: How often the manager and employee discuss progress, obstacles, and development.
aliases: How often would we discuss my progress?
Could we have regular development check-ins?
Would feedback be annual, twice yearly, or quarterly?

name: Teamwork in Performance Reviews
definition: The importance assigned to documented cooperation with colleagues when evaluating performance.
aliases: Would helping teammates count in my review?
Could cooperation be part of performance evaluation?
Would sales results be the only thing evaluated?

name: Quota Relief After Losing an Account
definition: The reduction in the next quota after the company removes a substantial share of assigned accounts.
aliases: What happens to my target if assigned accounts are taken away?
Could the next target be adjusted after a major account loss?
Would the adjustment match the accounts lost?

name: Notice before target changes
definition: The written notice required before a changed sales target takes effect.
aliases: How much warning would I get before my target changed?
Could target changes take effect immediately?
Would I have 30 or 60 days to adjust?

name: Early Customer Opportunities
definition: Customer opportunities with a stated need and agreed next step expected by day 90.
aliases: How many promising opportunities would I need early on?
Would there be a pipeline goal before full sales results are expected?
Could the early pipeline target be modest?

name: Probation Coaching Time
definition: Scheduled manager-coaching hours provided monthly when early performance concerns arise.
aliases: How much coaching would be available if I struggled early?
Could we schedule regular time to review performance?
Would coaching take time away from selling?

name: Time to Respond to a Review
definition: The time allowed to submit a written response after receiving a negative performance review.
aliases: Could I respond before a negative review becomes final?
How long would I have to explain my side?
Would a written response be included in my review?

name: When Review Standards Are Set
definition: When written performance standards used in evaluation are provided to the employee.
aliases: When would I learn what my review is based on?
Could standards be set before the review period starts?

name: Evidence for Poor Performance
definition: Documentation required before concluding that performance is below expectations.
aliases: What evidence would be used if performance became a concern?
Could one manager impression determine the outcome?

name: Pipeline Credit After Reassignment
definition: How documented opportunity credit is divided after account or territory ownership changes.
aliases: Who gets credit if my accounts change?
What happens to deals already underway?
Can existing opportunities remain partly mine?
choices: Previous owner keeps agreed credit for active opportunities
Previous owner keeps credit until the next milestone

name: Fair Lead Assignment
definition: How qualified inbound leads are assigned and whether salespeople can understand the allocation rule.
aliases: Can I understand the assignment rule?
What happens when an assignment seems unusual?
choices: Manager decides without a written rule
Written rule plus explanations for exceptions

name: Lead Workload Limits
definition: Whether new qualified leads pause when active workload exceeds an agreed capacity.
aliases: Can new leads pause if I am overloaded?
Is there a clear workload limit?
Who can approve a temporary pause?
choices: Automatic pause at the agreed workload limit

name: Starting Sales Area
definition: The written territory, customer segment, or account group assigned initially.
aliases: Which customers or area would I start with?
Would my starting accounts be clearly defined?
Who gets ordinary opportunities in my area?
choices: Written sales area with priority on ordinary opportunities

name: Lead Response Time
definition: The maximum working-hours response time expected after receiving a qualified lead.
aliases: How quickly must I respond to a qualified lead?
Is response time measured in working hours?

name: Territory Sales Training
definition: The level of territory-specific information and guidance provided before the candidate begins selling.
aliases: What would I learn about my customers first?
Would I meet a manager before selling?
choices: Written briefing plus one manager meeting

name: Inactive Account Review
definition: The agreed inactivity trigger for deciding when an account may be reassigned.
aliases: When can an inactive account be reassigned?
What counts as meaningful account activity?
Is there an agreed inactivity period?

name: Priority Account Handoff
definition: Whether the outgoing salesperson introduces the incoming salesperson to a high-priority customer.
aliases: Would the previous salesperson introduce me?
How would a customer handoff begin?

name: Urgent Customer Backup
definition: Whether a named backup handles urgent customer problems when the candidate needs help or is unavailable.
aliases: Who backs me up on urgent customer problems?
Would someone cover when I am unavailable?
Who takes the lead during an urgent issue?
choices: Backup leads urgent problems and keeps the candidate informed

name: Notice Before Territory Changes
definition: The advance notice required before a non-emergency territory or account reassignment takes effect.
aliases: How much warning comes before account changes?
When would a territory change start?
Would non-emergency changes be announced ahead of time?

name: Routine Discount Limit
definition: The largest routine customer discount the candidate may approve without manager approval.
aliases: I want to handle ordinary discounts without asking every time.
The company should protect margins while giving me room to learn. ]},{

name: Authority Growth Review
definition: How the company decides whether to increase the candidate’s routine commercial authority after initial performance.
aliases: I want to know how stronger decision authority will be considered.
The review should use results I can actually influence. ]},{
choices: Authority grows after a stated performance threshold

name: Deal Approval Rules
definition: Which customer-deal decisions require internal approval before the candidate proceeds.
aliases: I need clear boundaries for when another person must approve a deal.
Routine customer work should not stop because every unusual detail needs review. ]},{
choices: Approval is required for discounts or unusual terms
Approval is required only beyond stated limits
Candidate may approve routine deals within stated limits

name: Routine Deal Ownership
definition: Which routine sales stages the candidate may manage independently without manager approval.
aliases: I want to own ordinary customer work from first conversation through proposal.
Management can keep final control of unusual or binding commitments. ]},{
choices: Candidate and manager share routine deal decisions
Candidate leads routine deals within stated limits

name: Coaching on Pricing and Deal Decisions
definition: How much guided practice the candidate receives on pricing, discount, and deal-approval decisions before handling those decisions independently.
aliases: I learn faster when someone reviews realistic decisions with me.
A little coaching before independence could prevent expensive mistakes. ]},{
choices: No guided practice on pricing or deal decisions
One guided pricing or deal case during onboarding
Monthly guided reviews of pricing or deal decisions

name: Specialist Help Response Time
definition: The maximum business-hour wait for a named specialist to respond when a customer deal needs specialist input.
aliases: I need to know how long expert help will take on an important deal.
Specialist support should be predictable without taking over someone else’s workload. ]},{

name: Temporary Authority Review
definition: When a temporary reduction in the candidate’s routine authority must be reviewed.
aliases: If my authority changes temporarily, I want to know when it will be reconsidered.
A review date is different from a promise that authority must be restored. ]},{

name: Manager Absence Backup
definition: Who may decide routine customer matters when the candidate’s usual manager is unavailable.
aliases: I should not have to pause routine customer work whenever my manager is away.
A backup can handle ordinary decisions without taking over unusual ones. ]},{
choices: No named backup can decide routine matters
A named backup gives advice but cannot decide
A named backup may decide routine matters

name: Customer Account Ownership
definition: Which customer accounts the candidate may manage independently without manager approval.
aliases: I want clear ownership of the customers I am expected to develop.
Customers should know who is responsible for their ordinary account needs.
choices: Candidate manages all accounts in the assigned territory

name: Pay Review Timing
definition: When pay is reviewed after an approved promotion, without guaranteeing a pay increase.
aliases: When would my pay be reviewed after promotion?
Would the pay discussion happen before new responsibilities begin?
I want the timing of any promotion-related pay review to be clear.

name: Advancement Review Frequency
definition: How often the company formally reviews readiness for advancement, without guaranteeing promotion.
aliases: How often would we discuss readiness for advancement?
I would prefer a regular promotion-readiness review schedule.
Would advancement reviews happen annually or twice yearly?

name: Temporary Lead Assignment Length
definition: The maximum length of one temporary assignment leading a sales team.
aliases: Could I lead the team temporarily to build leadership experience?
How long would a temporary team-lead assignment last?
A longer trial leadership role would help demonstrate readiness.

name: Written Promotion Criteria
definition: The written evidence and capabilities used to judge readiness for promotion, without making promotion automatic.
aliases: What evidence would show that I am ready for promotion?
I would value written standards rather than informal judgment alone.
Would sales and customer results be part of the promotion decision?

name: Professional Development Budget
definition: The annual amount available for approved courses, certifications, or other role-related development.
aliases: Would the company pay for relevant courses or certifications?
How much development funding would be available each year?
I would value training that improves my sales skills.

name: Protected Development Time
definition: Paid work time reserved during the first 18 months for one defined assignment outside normal sales duties.
aliases: Would paid work time be set aside for development?
How much time could I spend on a cross-functional learning assignment?
I do not want development added on top of my sales workload.

name: Cross-Team Project Opportunities
definition: The number of company projects outside the sales team the employee may join each year.
aliases: Could I join projects outside the sales team?
How many cross-team projects could I participate in each year?
I would value experience with other teams.

name: Promotion Eligibility Timing
definition: When the candidate first becomes eligible for promotion consideration, without guaranteeing promotion.
aliases: When could I first be considered for promotion?
Would eligibility begin after six or twelve months?
I want the earliest consideration date to be clear.

name: Use of Work Achievements
definition: What factual, nonconfidential skills and achievements the candidate may mention in resumes and interviews after leaving.
aliases: Could I describe my results on a future resume?
What achievements could I mention after leaving?
I want to use factual, nonconfidential accomplishments in interviews.

name: Senior Career Guidance
definition: The number of yearly career-development conversations with a designated senior employee lacking promotion authority.
aliases: Could I speak with a senior employee about career development?
How often would those conversations happen?
I would value advice outside my direct reporting line.

name: Protected Training Hours
definition: Paid work time reserved during the first 90 days for learning the role.
aliases: How many paid work hours are reserved for learning during my first 90 days?
I would like training time protected from sales targets.{

name: Customer System Practice
definition: The number of supervised practice sessions before independently using the customer-record system.
aliases: How many supervised practice sessions would I get before using customer records independently?
Could I practice in a safe training environment first?
I do not want to make customer-record mistakes while learning.
choices: No supervised practice before independent use
One supervised practice session before independent use
Three supervised practice sessions before independent use

name: Early Progress Reviews
definition: Scheduled conversations during the first 90 days about learning progress and next steps.
aliases: How many progress conversations would we have during my first 90 days?
I would rather fix problems early than discover them at the end of onboarding.ρ?]}]}

name: Customer Readiness Check
definition: The method used to decide whether the candidate may independently handle customer opportunities.
aliases: How would we decide whether I am ready to handle customers alone?
I would want the standard based on the actual job.
Would the assessment use realistic customer situations?
choices: Manager judgment without a defined assessment

name: Customer Calls to Observe
definition: The number of suitable customer calls observed before independently leading calls.
aliases: How many customer calls could I observe before leading my own?
Seeing different customer situations would help me learn.
Too much observation could delay my contribution.

name: Mentor Meeting Frequency
definition: The minimum frequency of scheduled one-to-one meetings with an experienced colleague during the first 90 days.
aliases: Would I have a regular mentor or experienced colleague during onboarding?
How often could I discuss practical questions with someone experienced?
A consistent contact would help me build useful relationships.

name: Certification Fee Support
definition: The amount reimbursed for one approved, role-related external certification.
aliases: Would the company help pay for a certification related to the job?
How much would I have to pay myself?
A credential could help my future career.

name: Notice of Sales Process Changes
definition: Time allowed to notify the candidate in writing about material product or sales-process changes.
aliases: How quickly would I receive written notice of important sales changes?
I would want written guidance instead of relying on rumors or memory.
What counts as a material change?
choices: Written notice within five business days
Written notice within two business days

name: Online Learning Access
definition: The level of access to current role-related courses after initial onboarding.
aliases: Would I retain access to role-related courses after onboarding?
Could I learn new skills without waiting for a formal class?
What online training would be available?

name: Weekend Work Frequency
definition: The maximum number of Saturday or Sunday days the candidate must work during a typical quarter.

name: Paid Learning Time
definition: Paid work hours reserved each week for an agreed training or mentoring activity.

name: After-Hours Event Frequency
definition: The maximum number of required company, recruiting, or client events outside working hours each quarter.

name: Within-Week Schedule Flexibility
definition: The amount of scheduled work time the candidate may move to another day within the same workweek.

name: Team Overlap Hours
definition: The fixed number of hours each workday when the candidate must be available for team and customer collaboration.

name: Late Internal Meetings
definition: The number of recurring internal meetings scheduled outside the candidate’s agreed ordinary working window each week.
choices: 2 or more late internal meetings each week
0 recurring late internal meetings each week

name: Schedule Change Notice
definition: The minimum notice the company must give before changing an already agreed working period.

name: Weekly Extra-Duty Hours
definition: The maximum paid work time each week assigned to approved duties outside the candidate’s direct sales work.

name: Schedule Publication Notice
definition: How many calendar days before an ordinary work period the company must publish that schedule.

name: Initial Focus Period
definition: Weeks after starting when core duties are protected from supplementary assignments.

name: Travel Payment Timing
definition: When the company pays approved travel costs that the employee would otherwise pay personally.
aliases: When would I get travel money?
Would I need to use my own cash?

name: Supervised First Customer Visits
definition: Initial customer visits completed alongside an experienced colleague before working alone.
aliases: Would I go alone at first?
How many customer visits would be supervised?

name: Travel Approval Speed
definition: The maximum time a manager takes to answer a request for unusual business travel.
aliases: How quickly would travel requests be answered?
Would I be waiting days for approval?

name: Travel Notice
definition: The usual minimum notice before assigning unusual business travel, excluding genuine urgent customer needs.
aliases: How much warning would I get?
Would I have time to plan?

name: Overnight Travel Limit
definition: The normal maximum number of work-related overnight stays assigned in one calendar month.
aliases: How often would I sleep away from home?
Is there a monthly travel limit?
How many overnight trips are expected?

name: Travel Meal Reimbursement
definition: Maximum meal reimbursement for each eligible business-travel day.
aliases: Would meals be covered on trips?

name: Remote Customer Follow-Ups
definition: Who decides whether a routine customer follow-up can use video instead of an in-person visit.
aliases: Could routine check-ins happen by video?
Can I avoid unnecessary customer trips?

name: Fieldwork Travel Area
definition: The broadest geographic area where the employee normally performs customer fieldwork.
aliases: How far would I travel for customers?
Could I be sent anywhere in the country?

name: Paid Caregiving Days
definition: Extra paid workdays each year for caring for an ill, injured, or dependent family member.
unit: paid caregiving days per rolling 12 months
aliases: Paid days to care for family
Time off when someone at home is sick
Paid time for urgent family care

name: Recurring Schedule Flexibility
definition: The recurring choice of when to start and finish work while maintaining required client and team coverage.
aliases: Regular flexibility around school or care

name: Leave Coverage Plan
definition: The agreed coverage arrangement that keeps work covered while you are on planned leave.
aliases: I should not be contacted while away
A clear handoff before I leave

name: Unpaid Emergency Leave
definition: Extra unpaid days for urgent family-care needs, separate from other available leave.
unit: unpaid emergency family-leave days per rolling 12 months
aliases: Unpaid days for a family emergency
Time off after paid leave is used
A dependable option for urgent care

name: Post-Travel Recovery Time
definition: The allowed next-day start delay after an overnight trip ending after 10 p.m., with weekly hours unchanged.
aliases: A later start after a late trip
Do not start early after late travel

name: Four-Day Workweek Trial
definition: A trial allowing the same weekly hours across four longer days instead of the standard schedule.
aliases: Have a regular extra day off

name: Time to Approve Planned Leave
definition: Maximum response time for a planned-leave request.
aliases: Know when my leave request will be answered
Get a quick answer about planned time off
Plan ahead with a clear response

name: Alternative Travel for Care Needs
definition: The agreed response when required overnight travel conflicts with temporary caregiving, while essential coverage remains protected.
aliases: A solution when overnight travel clashes with care
Another way to cover a required trip

name: Gradual Return After Absence
definition: The pace for restoring normal sales workload after an absence of at least four weeks.
aliases: Have a lighter workload after a long absence

name: After-Hours Client Duty
definition: Whether the candidate personally responds to client requests outside normal working hours.
aliases: I do not want routine evening client calls.
I can cover urgent issues if expectations are clear. ]},{

name: Sales Forecast Reports
definition: How often the candidate submits a separate sales forecast report each month.
aliases: I would rather keep sales information current than send duplicate reports.
Weekly reporting seems reasonable if it is genuinely useful. ]},{

name: Sales Coaching Frequency
definition: How many scheduled coaching sessions the candidate receives per month during the first six months.
aliases: I would value regular feedback while learning the role.
A monthly check-in may not be enough when starting. ]},{

name: Core Sales System Access
definition: The company’s commitment to provide essential sales-system access by a specified start-time deadline.
aliases: I need access to essential sales systems when I start.
Delayed access would make it harder to become productive quickly. ]},{

name: Administrative Support Time
definition: Weekly staff time available to handle routine sales administration for the candidate.
aliases: I would like help with routine customer-system updates and scheduling.
Administrative support would leave more time for selling. ]},{

name: Written Onboarding Plan
definition: Whether the company provides a written schedule for the candidate’s initial training and work priorities.
aliases: I would like a clear plan for learning the products and role.
Knowing the first few months’ priorities would help. ]},{

name: Proposal Review Time
definition: The promised turnaround for internal review of proposals requiring more than an approved standard template.
aliases: Slow proposal reviews could make me look unresponsive to customers.
I would want a clear turnaround time for unusual proposals. ]},{

name: Company Card Access
definition: Whether approved sales expenses can be paid directly with a company card instead of the candidate's money.
aliases: I do not want to pay ordinary customer or travel costs myself.
A clear reimbursement timeline would make work expenses predictable. ]},{
choices: Company card for approved travel expenses
Company card for all approved sales expenses

name: Time to Correct Customer Records
definition: The promised deadline for correcting important errors in customer records after sales activity.
aliases: I would want a clear deadline for fixing important customer-record mistakes.
Errors affecting an active opportunity should be fixed quickly. ]},{

name: Work System Recovery Time
definition: The maximum target time for restoring the candidate’s ability to work after a critical sales-system failure.
aliases: I would need a clear time limit if a critical work system fails.
Being unable to work for several days would be a serious problem. ]},{

name: Written Handover Materials
definition: The written account information the employee must prepare before the final working day.
choices: Detailed notes for all active accounts and next actions

name: Notice Period Length
definition: The required notice between resignation and the final working day.

name: Use of Work Samples
definition: Whether the candidate may display approved, non-confidential work samples after employment ends.

name: Post-Departure Commissions
definition: Whether documented opportunities developed before departure can earn commission when they close afterward.
aliases: getting paid when a deal closes
choices: Only deals closed by the final workday

name: Future Employment Reference
definition: The information the company may provide to future employers about the candidate's past role.

name: Personal Contact Privacy
definition: Whether the company may share the employee's personal contact details after employment ends.

name: Client Transition Calls
definition: Approved client-transition calls the employee must join during notice.

name: Departure Announcement Notice
definition: The advance notice the candidate receives before the company announces the departure.

name: Departure Compensation
definition: A payment the company provides when employment ends, separate from earned wages and commissions.

name: Notice-Period Work Status
definition: The employee's work arrangement between giving notice and the final working day.
choices: Paid leave during the notice period

name: Recruiting Quote Approval
definition: Whether the company gets the candidate’s approval before publishing the candidate’s recruiting quote.
aliases: Can I approve quotes before publication?
Will the company use my words in recruiting materials?
Do I get to check public statements about me?

name: Declining Publicity Requests
definition: Whether the candidate may refuse nonessential publicity activities without punishment or lost ordinary work opportunities.
aliases: Can I say no to publicity?
Are public appearances part of the job?

name: Approval of Personal Profile Updates
definition: Whether the candidate may list the employer, role, dates, and nonconfidential skills on personal professional profiles.
aliases: Can I list this job on my profile?
Do I need approval to update my work history?
Can I describe the skills I use here?

name: Customer Story Attribution
definition: Whether an approved customer story names the candidate when their work materially contributed and the customer permits attribution.
aliases: Would my name appear in a customer success story?
Can I receive credit for work highlighted to a customer?
Who gets named in customer case studies?

name: Mentoring Assignment Choice
definition: Whether mentoring coworkers is an expected part of the candidate’s paid role.
aliases: Is mentoring coworkers part of the job?
Would mentoring receive dedicated work time?
How much coaching would I be expected to provide?

name: Paid Time for Publicity
definition: Whether voluntary, company-approved publicity work is completed during paid work time with a stated limit.
aliases: Would publicity work happen during paid hours?
How much work time would publicity activities take?
Would preparing a company story be unpaid?

name: Employee Referral Payment
definition: Whether a successful employee referral earns the candidate a fixed payment.
aliases: Is there a payment for referring someone?
Would a successful referral earn a bonus?
How much is the employee referral payment?

name: Reference Provider Choice

What will the company confirm about my performance?
choices: The former manager may provide the reference
Candidate chooses one approved senior colleague

name: Approval for Extra Assignments
definition: Who must approve work outside the candidate’s main sales responsibilities.
aliases: Who approves work outside my main sales role?
Can another department assign me work directly?

name: Role Review Schedule
definition: How often the candidate and manager formally review the candidate’s duties and priorities.
aliases: How often would we review what my job includes?
Would my priorities be reviewed regularly?
Could my responsibilities change without a scheduled review?

name: Primary Manager
definition: Whether one named manager is accountable for regular priorities and feedback.
aliases: Who would be my main manager?
Whose instructions take priority if managers disagree?

name: Input on Unusual Travel Dates
definition: Candidate input before the company confirms unusual customer-trip dates.
aliases: Would I be asked about conflicts before an unusual trip is booked?
Could I suggest another date for a customer visit?
Who makes the final call on unusual travel dates?

name: Sales Target Adjustment
definition: How approved non-sales work affects the candidate’s sales target when it displaces scheduled selling time.
aliases: What happens to my sales target if extra work takes selling time?
Would my quota change when I am assigned other duties?
Who decides whether my target is adjusted?

name: Resolving Work Conflicts
definition: Who decides which assignment takes priority when sales and cross-team work cannot both be completed on time.
aliases: Who decides what gets delayed when two teams need me?
What happens when cross-team work conflicts with selling?
Can managers agree which task takes priority?

name: Advance Notice of Product Changes
definition: How important product, price, or offer changes are communicated before customer use.
aliases: How would I hear about product or pricing changes?
Would I get updates before speaking with customers?
Could I receive a briefing on important product changes?

name: Customer Ownership After Handoff
definition: Whether the candidate remains responsible for the commercial relationship after operational work moves to another team.
aliases: Do I stay responsible for the customer after operations takes over?
Who owns the relationship after handoff?
When can the company move a customer to someone else?

name: Customer Promise Review
definition: Unusual customer promises receive a defined level of internal review before the candidate makes them.

Would a manager or specialist review unusual wording?

name: Complaint Support

aliases: If a customer is seriously unhappy, who takes over?

Who owns a serious complaint after I report it?

name: Customer Data Access While Traveling

Will I have an approved way to work remotely?
Can I use a company device for customer data?
choices: No approved access to necessary customer data while traveling
Access only through a company-managed device
Secure remote access through an approved company system

name: Customer Story Permission
definition: Customer permission is obtained before the company uses an identifiable customer story or reference.
aliases: Can I use a customer’s name or results in a pitch?
Who confirms that a customer agreed to be a reference?
Can the customer limit where its story appears?

name: Specialist Help for Customer Questions
definition: The candidate can send unanswered customer questions to a qualified internal specialist.
aliases: What happens when a customer asks something I cannot answer?
Can I consult someone qualified on technical questions?
Who helps with sensitive customer questions?

name: Performance-Based Progression
definition: Scheduled decision about broader responsibilities after agreed performance targets are met.
aliases: I want a clear path to progress.
I do not need promotion promised automatically. ]},{
choices: No progression review occurs during the contract
Progression is discussed during the annual review
Meeting agreed targets triggers a progression decision

name: Planned Schedule Changes for Family Needs
definition: Agreed alternative work schedule for recurring family periods.
aliases: I need predictable flexibility at certain times of year.
I can plan schedule changes in advance. ]},{
choices: No alternative schedule applies during recurring family periods
Two recurring family periods may use advance-planned schedule changes
Four recurring family periods may use advance-planned schedule changes

name: Target-based pay increase
definition: A fixed-pay increase granted after the candidate meets an agreed sales target.
aliases: I want more fixed pay if I hit the target.
The increase should depend on measurable results. ]},{

name: Performance Improvement Period
definition: Time allowed to improve after missing an agreed sales target before stronger employment action is considered.
aliases: I need income security while building my accounts.
I understand early sales may take time. ]},{

name: Maximum Active Accounts
definition: The maximum number of customer accounts assigned to the candidate at one time.
aliases: I want a limit on how many accounts I handle.
A larger portfolio may help cover more customers. ]},{

name: Sales Shadowing Time
definition: Paid time during the first six months for observing experienced customer work.
aliases: I want paid time to learn the products and sales process.
Training should help me become productive quickly. ]},{

name: Contract Renewal Notice
definition: How far before a fixed-term contract ends the company communicates its current renewal intention.
aliases: I want enough warning to plan my next step.
The company may need time to assess business needs.
choices: No notice before the contract ends

name: Reply Times During the Workday
definition: The response standard for routine and urgent work messages during agreed working hours, excluding evenings, weekends, leave, and other unavailable periods.
aliases: Can routine messages have a same-day response expectation rather than an immediate one?
Let’s use one defined channel for genuinely urgent customer matters.
A scheduled focus block should pause the routine response clock.
choices: Routine work messages require a response within 1 hour during working hours, with no separate urgent channel.
Routine work messages receive a response within the same working day, and urgent customer matters use one agreed escalation channel.
Routine work messages receive a response within 1 business day, and urgent customer matters use one agreed escalation channel; the clock pauses during a scheduled focus block.

name: Weekly No-Meeting Focus Time
definition: The amount of recurring weekly time reserved for uninterrupted individual work, subject only to defined urgent customer or team exceptions.
aliases: Could one recurring 90-minute block be protected for focused work?
Two blocks would help me keep routine work from consuming personal time.
Urgent customer or team decisions could remain exceptions.
choices: No recurring weekly focus time is protected from routine internal meetings.
One 90-minute recurring focus block is protected each week, except for urgent customer or team decisions.
Two recurring 90-minute focus blocks are protected each week, except for urgent customer or team decisions.

name: Notice of Internal Job Openings
definition: Whether the candidate receives timely notice of relevant internal vacancies and may apply without selection priority.
aliases: Could relevant internal openings be shared with me after six months in good standing?
I am asking for notice, not priority over other applicants.
Would five business days’ notice be workable once I am eligible?
choices: The candidate learns of internal vacancies only through the standard public internal-posting channel.
After six months in good standing, the company sends the candidate notice of internal openings that reasonably match the candidate’s skills before the application deadline.
After three months in good standing, the company sends the candidate notice of relevant internal job openings at least five business days before the application deadline.

name: Time Credit for Teaching Colleagues
definition: When peer teaching is assigned, its session length and preparation time are scheduled within working hours, with an identified work task deferred if necessary.
aliases: If peer teaching is assigned, can preparation time be scheduled within my work plan?
Could we set a maximum session length and identify which sales task moves if there is a conflict?
I am open to quarterly teaching if the preparation and workload tradeoff are explicit.
choices: Peer teaching and preparation are added to the normal sales workload without a time limit or adjustment to other priorities.
The manager schedules one short peer-teaching session per quarter, allows up to one hour of preparation during work time, and reviews competing priorities.
Each session has an agreed topic and maximum duration, preparation time is scheduled in advance, and a lower-priority sales task is explicitly deferred when teaching creates a conflict.

name: Respecting Customer Do-Not-Contact Requests
definition: The company records a prospect’s contact refusal in the CRM, assigns ownership for follow-up, and suppresses further company outreach through the designated workflow.
aliases: Where do I record a prospect’s opt-out in the CRM?
Who owns suppression after I enter the refusal?
Can an opt-out automatically stop future outreach and show that it was completed?
choices: The candidate keeps opt-outs in personal notes or memory, and the CRM has no defined owner or suppression step.
The candidate records an opt-out in the CRM and routes it to the named owner within one business day for manual suppression.
A required CRM field triggers automatic suppression, records completion, and provides an escalation route when suppression cannot be completed promptly.

name: Customer Contact Hours
definition: The normal customer-facing availability window the candidate must provide for customers outside the candidate’s local working region, excluding general core hours and emergency-contact rules.
aliases: Which customer region is the primary coverage responsibility?
Could we use one fixed eight-hour window with only a few planned exceptions?
Are early or late customer calls occasional exceptions or a regular expectation?
choices: Provide customer-facing availability from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. in the candidate’s local time on each normal workday for the identified customer regions.
Provide one fixed eight-hour customer-facing window aligned with the primary customer region, plus no more than four planned early or late exceptions per quarter with five business days’ notice.
Provide customer-facing availability only from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. in the candidate’s local time, with no recurring early or late coverage requirement.

name: Information Included With New Leads
definition: For leads generated through company campaigns, the candidate receives relevant source and context information and knows the responsible internal contact for follow-up questions.
aliases: Could campaign leads include their source and any relevant context?
Who should I contact if the lead information is incomplete?
I am asking for usable handoff information, not control over lead allocation.
choices: The candidate receives a campaign-generated lead with no source, context, or identified contact and must reconstruct the information independently.
Marketing provides the lead source and available relevant context when the lead is passed to the candidate, with one named contact for questions.

Every campaign-generated lead is passed with its source and relevant customer context, and a named marketing contact is available for prompt clarification without changing lead ownership or allocation.

name: Time Spent Sharing Knowledge
definition: The amount of work time the candidate must spend documenting lessons or handing off practices to colleagues.
aliases: Would you expect any defined time for documenting account lessons?
Could we start with four work hours per quarter for peer handoffs?
If knowledge sharing is required, it should occur during work time rather than adding an uncapped duty.
choices: No defined knowledge-sharing contribution beyond ordinary informal communication.
Spend up to 4 work hours per quarter documenting useful account lessons or completing one approved peer handoff.
Spend 12 protected work hours per quarter documenting practices and delivering two approved peer handoffs.

name: Post-Trip Reporting Requirements
definition: The amount and timing of required post-trip reporting for customer travel.
aliases: What report is required after a customer trip?
Can one concise template replace a detailed narrative?
Can routine trips be reported in a weekly consolidated form?
choices: Every trip requires a detailed narrative, duplicate data entry, and a report within one business day regardless of trip purpose.
Each trip requires one concise expense and customer-outcome record using the company template within five business days.
Only material expenses and the key customer outcome are recorded once through a shared form within five business days; recurring or routine trips may use a consolidated weekly report.

name: Travel Booking and Connection Times
definition: The maximum practical burden of itinerary connections and departure or arrival times when a reasonably comparable lower-cost option exists.
aliases: Could the company avoid more than one connection when the practical option is within 10% of the lowest fare?
Can we set a departure and arrival boundary for non-routine trips?
What itinerary price difference is acceptable for avoiding an overnight or extreme travel time?
choices: The company may select the lowest-cost itinerary regardless of the number of connections or departure and arrival times.
For non-routine travel, the company avoids more than one connection or an overnight journey when a reasonably comparable option costs no more than 10% extra.
For non-routine travel, the company avoids more than one connection and departures before 6:00 a.m. or arrivals after 10:00 p.m. when a reasonably comparable option costs no more than 15% extra.

name: Sales Support Response Time
definition: The company-controlled process for routing defined sales-operations requests to a named owner with stated response targets.
aliases: Can defined sales-operations requests go through one named queue?
What acknowledgement time applies to a live customer deal?
If the final answer is delayed, can the queue provide a holding response and escalation?
choices: The candidate sends quoting, scheduling, or sales-system requests through informal channels with no named sales-operations owner or response target.

A named sales-operations queue covers routine quoting, scheduling, and sales-system requests, acknowledges them within one business day, and gives a substantive response or status within three business days.

The same queue provides an urgent live-deal category, assigns an owner within four working hours, and gives a same-day answer or documented holding response; it does not guarantee another department’s final decision.

name: Who Handles Overlapping Prospects
definition: The process for assigning a duplicate or clearly cross-boundary prospect to one accountable owner while preserving a clean handoff.
aliases: For a cross-boundary prospect, I need one recorded owner and a direct introduction.
Could a designated manager resolve duplicate records within two business days?
I can make one continuity introduction, but ownership and compensation should be recorded separately.
choices: The candidate forwards a disputed or cross-boundary prospect to management, which decides ownership case by case without a stated response time.
A designated sales-operations or manager contact confirms the owner within two business days, records the decision, and supports a direct introduction to the new owner.

The owner is confirmed promptly from a written routing rule, the duplicate record is resolved, and the candidate may make one documented continuity introduction before handoff without retaining compensation or decision rights.

name: Raising Concerns About Sales Practices
definition: A salesperson can document and promptly escalate a good-faith concern about potentially misleading or unsuitable sales conduct through a named internal review route, without deciding legal rights or excusing misconduct.
aliases: What is the named channel for documenting a good-faith concern about a sales claim?
Could urgent concerns receive same-day acknowledgment and a clear status update?
Who reviews a concern when the immediate deal manager is involved?
choices: The candidate is expected to proceed with a questionable sales action and has no named route or expected response for raising a concern.
The candidate records a good-faith concern in the designated channel; a named manager acknowledges it within two business days and provides a decision or status update within five.

A good-faith concern about a potentially misleading or unsuitable sales practice is logged before the affected action where practicable, receives same-day acknowledgment when urgent, and may be reviewed by a manager outside the immediate deal.

name: What Counts as a Qualified Lead
definition: The objective criteria used to classify an inquiry as a qualified sales opportunity before it is assigned to the candidate.
aliases: Let’s agree what makes an inquiry an active opportunity before it counts toward my workload.
Could fit, need, and a reachable contact be the basic threshold?
For stronger qualification, we could record the buying timeframe and decision-maker, while keeping exceptions visible.
choices: Any inbound inquiry may be assigned as an active opportunity, with no agreed criteria for need, fit, or buying readiness.
An active opportunity must meet agreed basic criteria for customer fit, identified need, and a reachable contact; borderline inquiries are labeled for review rather than counted as qualified.
An active opportunity must meet the middle criteria plus a documented buying timeframe and identified decision-maker, with exceptions recorded by the manager.

name: Support After a Sale
definition: The candidate completes specified customer handoff materials and provides limited post-handoff support for a defined period before responsibility moves to the named implementation or customer-success owner.
aliases: I can provide a written handoff and answer transition questions for two weeks.
Could the receiving implementation owner be named when responsibility transfers?
I want post-sale support to be bounded rather than indefinite.
choices: After closing, the candidate remains the informal contact for post-sale questions with no defined handoff deliverable, owner, or end date.
The candidate gives the implementation owner an agreed written summary and answers reasonable transition questions for up to two weeks after the handoff.

The candidate gives a concise written brief, makes one introduction, and answers reasonable transition questions for up to two weeks; the handoff record names the receiving owner and confirms transfer of responsibility.

name: Travel Class for Long Trips
definition: The permitted class for a one-way business flight lasting more than four scheduled hours, if the role requires such travel.
aliases: If the role involves flights over four hours, what class applies?
Could premium economy apply to those one-way flights?
Would overnight travel or a medical exception be handled separately?
choices: Economy class for every qualifying flight.
Premium economy for one-way flights exceeding four scheduled hours.
Business class for one-way flights exceeding four scheduled hours.

name: Written Reasons for Promotion Decisions
definition: Whether the candidate receives written reasons and a follow-up discussion when a requested promotion is not approved.
aliases: If advancement is not approved, could I receive brief written reasons and a follow-up conversation?
Could the reasons identify the skills I would need to demonstrate next?
I do not need an appeal right or a guarantee of promotion.
choices: A promotion denial is communicated without written reasons or a follow-up discussion.
Within 30 days of a denial, the manager provides brief written reasons and offers one follow-up discussion.
Within 30 days of a denial, the manager provides written reasons tied to documented expectations and holds a follow-up discussion with HR or a second manager present.

name: Notice Before Sales Meetings
definition: Relevant internal meetings involving the candidate ordinarily provide enough advance notice and a clear purpose for the candidate to prepare and protect selling time.
aliases: Could relevant sales meetings include an agenda one business day ahead?
I need to know the purpose before protecting time for a meeting.
If my attendance is not necessary, may I send written input instead?
choices: The candidate is routinely added to internal meetings without a clear sales-related purpose or usable notice.
Relevant internal meetings ordinarily include a stated purpose and agenda at least one business day in advance.
Relevant internal meetings ordinarily include a purpose, agenda, and materials at least 48 hours in advance, with written input accepted when the candidate’s attendance is not necessary.

name: Periods With No Overnight Travel
definition: A limited number of dates or date ranges designated in advance during which the candidate will not normally be scheduled for required overnight business travel.
aliases: Could we identify two family periods each year when overnight travel will not normally be scheduled?
I can provide the dates 60 days in advance.
For a broader arrangement, I would ask for four capped periods with an emergency exception.
choices: No dates are protected from required overnight travel.
Two designated periods of up to five consecutive calendar days each are protected annually, with dates supplied at least 60 days in advance.
Four designated periods of up to seven consecutive calendar days each are protected annually, with dates supplied at least 60 days in advance.

name: Rules for Customer Gifts
definition: A customer gift or personal relationship that could reasonably influence a sales decision is disclosed through a named internal channel and reviewed before the candidate continues or is reassigned.
aliases: What customer gifts or relationships must I disclose?
Who reviews a disclosed conflict, and how quickly?
Can the decision about continuing or stepping away from the opportunity be recorded?
choices: The candidate decides privately whether a customer gift or relationship matters and continues the opportunity without disclosure.
A gift above the agreed modest-value threshold or a potentially influencing relationship is logged with the manager, who reviews it within two business days.
The company provides written examples and a documented approval route; the reviewer records whether the candidate may continue, needs conditions, or must step away.

name: Access to Customer References
definition: Access to authorized, non-confidential customer examples for preparing sales conversations.
aliases: Will I have an approved library of customer examples for sales preparation?
Who confirms whether a reference is authorized for a particular prospect?
Can priority opportunities receive a faster reference-material response?
choices: The candidate has no company-provided reference library and must independently locate examples without guidance on authorization or confidentiality.

The company provides a searchable set of approved, anonymized or consented customer examples and identifies a contact who can confirm whether an example is suitable for a specific opportunity within three business days.
The library is current and searchable, includes multiple examples by use case, and the named contact responds to priority-opportunity requests within one business day where practicable.

name: Approval for Needed Sales Tools
definition: The company-controlled process for requesting and testing a low-cost, role-critical sales tool after security and customer-data review.
aliases: Who decides whether a role-critical low-cost tool is approved?
Can approved costs be paid or reimbursed rather than personally absorbed?
Could a security-approved, no-customer-data tool be trialed for 30 days?
choices: Requests for a role-critical tool have no stated decision owner or turnaround, and the candidate may not use an unapproved service or enter customer data into it.
A manager and security owner give a written approve, reject, or information-needed decision within ten business days; approved costs are paid or reimbursed by the company under its normal process.
The same process permits a 30-day trial of an approved tool that handles no customer data, with a named owner, documented security decision, and cancellation or renewal review before the trial ends.

name: Credit in Internal Project Records
definition: Whether a completed internal project or process-improvement record identifies the candidate when the candidate made a verified substantial contribution.
aliases: Could completed project records identify me when my manager verifies a substantial contribution?
I am asking for factual internal attribution, not authorship or extra compensation.
Would a standard contribution field make this easy to administer?
choices: Internal project and process records identify only the team or department; no individual-contribution field is used.
For each completed project or adopted process improvement, the manager records the candidate’s name and a factual role description when the manager verifies a substantial contribution.

The company uses a standard contribution field in every completed project or adopted process-improvement record, and the manager records the candidate’s verified substantial contribution within 30 days.

name: Private Hotel Room
definition: Whether the employer provides a private sleeping room for each required overnight business trip, using its standard booking or reimbursement process.
aliases: For required overnight trips, I need a private room rather than shared accommodation.
A private room within the normal travel budget would be a reasonable compromise.
If no suitable room is available near the work site, I would like to approve the alternative before booking.
choices: Shared sleeping accommodation may be used whenever it is the lowest-cost practical option.
A private room is provided in an ordinary business hotel or equivalent lodging within the employer’s standard travel budget.
A private room is provided for every required overnight trip, with location reasonably close to the work site; if unavailable, the candidate may approve the alternative before booking.

name: Career Path Review
definition: The scheduled reconsideration process when a specifically discussed development opportunity becomes unavailable, without guaranteeing promotion or an equivalent replacement.
aliases: If the discussed opportunity disappears, can we schedule a career-development discussion within 30 days?
I am not asking for a guaranteed promotion; I would like an agreed next development step.
We can revisit the plan, provided the alternative action remains subject to business needs and performance.
choices: If the discussed development opportunity becomes unavailable, there is no scheduled reconsideration.
The manager explains the change and schedules one career-development discussion within 30 days.
The manager explains the change, schedules one career-development discussion within 30 days, and records one mutually agreed alternative development action.

name: Travel Safety and Emergency Support
definition: The company’s disclosure of applicable business-travel procedures, policy terms, and an emergency contact before required overnight or unusual travel.
aliases: What travel-safety guidance and policy terms will I receive before an overnight trip?
Who is the urgent travel contact?
What additional process applies to an unusual destination?
choices: Before required travel, the company provides no travel-safety guidance, does not identify an emergency contact, and does not disclose the applicable business-travel policy terms.

Before the first overnight trip, the company gives the employee its standard travel-safety guidance, identifies an urgent-problem contact, and discloses the applicable insurance-policy terms and exclusions.

Before each unusual or higher-risk destination, the company provides destination-specific guidance, confirms the emergency escalation route, and arranges any required support consistent with law and the applicable policy; it does not guarantee coverage beyond the policy terms.

name: Accessible Sales Materials
definition: The company supplies customer-facing sales materials that meet an agreed accessibility and usability standard before the candidate uses them with customers.
aliases: Which customer-facing sales materials will the company provide before I begin selling?
What accessibility and usability standard will the approved materials meet?
Will new proposal packs be checked before I use them with customers?
choices: The candidate must create or adapt customer-facing materials independently, with no agreed accessibility or usability standard.
The company supplies approved customer-facing materials that meet a stated accessibility and usability standard before the candidate uses them.
The company supplies approved materials and records a documented pre-release check against the agreed standard for each new customer-facing pack.

name: Confidential Information Rules
definition: What non-public company and customer information the candidate must keep confidential, and which reasonable exclusions apply.
choices: Protect non-public business and customer information, with exclusions for public, prior, and independently developed knowledge
Protect any work-related information indefinitely, including remembered know-how

name: Contract Renewal Standards
definition: The written standards and discussion used to decide whether a fixed-term contract will be renewed.
choices: Recruiter decides without written standards or a review meeting
Written performance and conduct standards, with a renewal meeting before expiry
Automatic renewal unless there is serious misconduct

name: Expense Approval Rules
definition: Which work expenses need approval before purchase, separate from the amount of the personal budget.
choices: Only expenses above $500 need advance approval; routine policy-compliant expenses do not
No advance approval within the agreed personal budget

name: Customer and Employee Non-Solicitation
definition: Whether and for how long the candidate may approach customers or employees after leaving, without preventing all competing employment.
choices: For 6 months, do not solicit named customers directly served in the role
For 12 months, do not solicit any customer, prospect, or employee

name: Training Cost Repayment
definition: Whether the candidate must repay specified external training fees after voluntarily leaving, and how quickly that amount falls over time.
choices: Repay all training costs after leaving voluntarily within 24 months
Repay only documented external course fees, declining to zero over 12 months

name: Ownership of Work Created in the Role
definition: Who owns materials created for the job and what happens to work the candidate created before employment or outside the role.
choices: Company owns all related work created at any time, including prior and personal work
Company owns work created within the role using company time, information, or resources; prior and personal work is excluded
Candidate owns all work and gives the company a continuing right to use it

name: Reference and Background Checks
definition: The scope, consent, and relevance of checks completed before employment begins.
choices: Standard role-relevant checks with notice and consent
Broad checks unrelated to the role, with no clear completion date

name: Outside Work and Conflicts of Interest
definition: How the candidate discloses outside sales work or financial interests that could conflict with company or customer duties.
choices: No disclosure of outside interests or conflicting sales work
Confidentially disclose actual conflicts and outside sales work for case-by-case review
Ban all paid or unpaid outside activity

name: Return of Company Equipment and Information
definition: What the candidate must return or delete at the end of employment and how that process is documented.
choices: No documented return or deletion process
Return company devices and records and delete company copies using a written last-day checklist
Company may inspect and erase the candidate's personal devices and accounts

name: Regular Review of System Access
definition: Whether access to customer and company systems is periodically checked and limited to what the role needs.
choices: Quarterly role-based check that removes access no longer needed
Constant monitoring of personal activity as part of the access review

name: Required Sales Compliance Training
definition: The paid, role-relevant training the candidate completes on customer claims, privacy, gifts, and other sales rules.
choices: Concise paid training on the role's customer, privacy, gift, and claims rules
The candidate must complete lengthy unpaid sales-compliance training on topics unrelated to the role.

name: Written First-Week Schedule
definition: Whether the candidate receives a written schedule for the first week before the job begins.
choices: No written first-week schedule is provided before starting
A written first-week schedule is provided at least three days before starting

name: Unpaid Off-Hours Training
definition: Whether required training may be scheduled outside normal working hours without pay.
choices: All required training takes place during paid working time
Required training may be scheduled outside working hours without pay

name: Standard Weekly Working Hours
definition: The normal number of paid working hours expected each week, excluding exceptional overtime.

name: Paid Sick Days
definition: The number of paid days available each year for the candidate's own illness or medical recovery.

name: Employer Retirement Contribution
definition: The employer contribution to the candidate's retirement plan as a percentage of salary.

name: Employer Health-Insurance Contribution
definition: The share of the candidate's health-insurance premium paid by the employer.

name: Work Mobile-Phone Allowance
definition: The annual amount provided for a mobile phone or service used for customer-facing work.

name: Commuting Support
definition: The annual employer payment toward ordinary commuting costs that are not business travel.

name: Annual Sales Target
definition: The annual amount of credited sales the candidate is expected to achieve after the initial ramp period.
unit: USD of credited sales per year

name: Maximum Customer Meetings Per Week
definition: The maximum number of scheduled customer meetings expected in an ordinary week.

name: Maximum Consecutive Travel Days
definition: The maximum number of consecutive calendar days in one required business trip.

name: Paid Parental Leave
definition: The number of paid weeks available after the birth, adoption, or placement of a child.

name: Company Car
definition: Whether the candidate receives access to a company vehicle for customer travel.
choices: Access to a shared pool car

name: Wellness or Gym Benefit
definition: The annual employer contribution toward a gym membership or other approved wellbeing activity.

name: Employer-Paid Life Insurance
definition: The amount of employer-paid life-insurance cover included with the job.
choices: Cover equal to one year of salary
Cover equal to two years of salary

name: Equity or Profit Sharing
definition: The Candidate's equity-equivalent ownership or share of company profits.

name: Role Scope or Job Title
definition: The formal job title and associated level of responsibility.

name: Contract-Renewal Bonus
definition: A one-time bonus paid only if the employment contract is renewed.

name: Dedicated Office or Workspace
definition: The Candidate's access to quiet or private workspace.

name: Employee Discount
definition: The discount employees receive on eligible company products or services.

name: Lunch Break Length
definition: The normal length of the Candidate's daily lunch break.

name: Paid Volunteering Days
definition: The number of paid workdays each year the Candidate may use for approved volunteering.

name: Permission to Work Abroad
definition: Whether and how long the Candidate may temporarily work from another country.
choices: Up to 10 days per year with approval
Up to 30 days per year with approval

name: Work Clothing Allowance
definition: The annual allowance for professional clothing used in customer-facing work.

name: Work Technology Upgrade Allowance
definition: The annual allowance for optional upgrades to the laptop, phone, or other technology used for client work, beyond standard equipment.

name: Team Coaching Responsibility
definition: Whether the Candidate has a recurring responsibility to coach colleagues, and when it begins.
choices: Coach one newer teammate after probation with protected time
Lead team coaching from the first month

name: Sales Planning Meeting Access
definition: The Candidate's access to meetings where sales priorities and plans are discussed.
aliases: seat at the monthly sales meeting
choices: Attend the monthly sales planning meeting
